designated pediatric facility equipped to provide definitive care for all critically ill or injured
children, including those requiring intensive care or specialty surgical services. Unlike an Advanced
Pediatric Receiving Center, which focuses on emergency stabilization and initial management, a
Comprehensive PedRC offers 24/7 in-house pediatric subspecialists, and advanced diagnostic and
therapeutic capa

Attachment B of this Policy.

[8] 410 IV.B.1.a.iv (Pediatric Receiving Center Standards): Procedure > Pediatric Receiving Center Standards > A designated PedRC shall meet all the following standards: > Hospital Facility and Services

emergency care, stabilization, transfer and transport.

creating firm pressure to the source of the bleeding. Remove the fingers holding
pressure and continue to pack the wound with gauze until no more gauze can be
placed in the wound. This packing should be tight in the wound and fill all voids,
so pressure is maintained to the source of the bleeding. If the wound is large
enough to accept multiple

enough to pack. Wound or laceration may not be potentially open to a body cavity
(chest, abdomen or flank). If wound or laceration is located on an extremity and
has major hemorrhage or is too large to pack, go directly go to tourniquet.
